raw:
[1] Elihu answered and said:

[2] Have you considered this as justice, saying, "My righteousness is before God"?

[3] For if you say, "What will He do for you? What will He take from your sin?"

[4] I will answer you with words, and your companions with you.

[5] Look to the heavens and see; and behold, the clouds are higher than you.

[6] If you have sinned, what will you do to Him? Or if your sins multiply, what will you do to Him?

[7] If you are righteous, what will you give to Him? Or who will receive a gift from your hand?

[8] To a man like yourself, your sin is reckoned; and to a human, your righteousness.

[9] From the many who are oppressed, they cry out; they raise their voices from numerous hands.

[10] Yet no one says, "Where is the God who made me, who gives songs in the night?

[11] Who has set me apart from the beasts of the earth and from the winged creatures of the sky?"

[12] There they cry out, and He does not answer, because of the arrogance of the wicked.

[13] Indeed, He does not listen to emptiness; and the Almighty does not look upon it.

[14] Though you say, "He will not judge according to your case, nor will He bring judgment before Him."

[15] And now, because He does not yet notice His anger, and does not know a great misstep.

[16] Job speaks emptily, his mouth is filled with ignorance, and his words are heavy with thoughtlessness.

---
Notes
- v. 10: The phrase "gives songs in the night" reflects the poetic imagery of divine provision and comfort, consistent with the Hebrew. 
- v. 13: The translation of "שַׁוְּא" as "emptiness" and "שַׁדַּי לֹא יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה" as "the Almighty does not look upon it" maintains the contrast between divine indifference and human expectation.
